subject: Print Slow, Even with Excluded Variables

messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Print Slow, Even with Excluded Variables
parts:
Print has an option to set include=FALSE, which means that the character vector passed to pars excludes the listed variables. I have some variables that are very large, so excluding them is natural. However, print is very slow, even with these large variables excluded.

I found it interesting that when I then run print a second time, removing one of the excluded variables (i.e., including it in the print operation), the call to print is essentially instantaneous. This suggests to me that all the results of print are calculated for all the variables upon it's first time being called. These results are then cached for any future call.

If this is a correct understanding of how it works, I suggest that the print command should only do the calculations necessary to print the results (it can still cache them for future use).

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Print Slow, Even with Excluded Variables
parts:
Hi John, this actually has to do with the summary method (called internally by print). Check out the use_cache argument to the summary method for stanfit objects (help(`summary,stanfit-method`)). Essentially, what's going on is that, by default, the first time you run summary (even if indirectly by calling print), if the use_cache argument is set to TRUE then it will compute the summary statistics for all parameters and generated quantities and then cache them so that all future times you call summary or print the output can be taken from the cached summaries instead of computed every time. This is a bit strange, but it's particularly useful for models with lots of parameters because instead of print and summary being slow every time, they are only slow the first time. To disable this you can set use_cache=FALSE when calling summary or when calling print (because print passes arguments to summary via ...). 

Hope that helps, 

Jonah
